title: Definiteness of the probability inner product
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution assigning positive mass to every point of $\Omega$, and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Define $\langle f,g\rangle_\pi=\sum_{x\in\Omega}\pi(x)f(x)g(x)$. Then $\langle f,f\rangle_\pi=0$ if and only if $f$ is identically zero.
hypotheses_covered: Every point of $\Omega$ has positive probability
